clue.text: He went astray: should have been collared

definitions.text: He went astray: should have been collared

parts.words: He went astray: should have been collared
parts.note: reads like a remark about a runaway man who ought to have been arrested, but describes a pet that wandered off and needed a collar and lead

explanation.surface: A fugitive who slipped away ought to have been nabbed by the police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Collared' means arrested in slang, which makes the clue sound like a criminal; it also means wearing a collar, as a pet does.
explanation.definitionFit: A missing pet that has wandered off is one that went astray, and a dog should wear a collar.

clue.text: Union trouble mounts and is continuing

indicators.note: in a down clue mounts means climbing upwards, so the word for trouble is read bottom to top

parts.note: to ail is to trouble
taken as written
on means continuing, as in carry on

explanation.surface: Labour unrest at a trade union grows and persists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounts' turns AIL upwards to LIA in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A liaison is a close connection or a love affair between two people.

clue.text: Used to be worn out from our cats

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of our cats are put out of order

explanation.surface: Our cats' fur used to get worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges OUR CATS. The definition is in the past tense because the garment is historical.
explanation.definitionFit: A surcoat was a loose robe knights wore over armour in the Middle Ages.

clue.text: Doctor put a foot on a selection of soldiers…

explanation.surface: A medic tends the foot of a soldier picked for duty.
explanation.definitionFit: A draft is a detachment of troops chosen for a particular duty.

clue.text: … one of whom ordered rereading

indicators.note: ordered means put in order, so the letters of rereading are arranged anew

explanation.surface: One of the troops was told to read it again.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this to 3-down: 'one of whom' means one of the soldiers. 'ordered' rearranges REREADING.
explanation.definitionFit: A Guards infantryman belongs to a regiment of soldiers, so he is one of them.

clue.text: Fed hundreds at war first but made very little

indicators.note: first says the D and WAR come before the word fed in the answer

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for five hundred, so it stands for hundreds
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone fed hundreds of troops in wartime yet produced very little food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' is the indicator: the hundreds and the war come before the feeding, though the clue opens on 'Fed'. D for hundreds rests on D = 500.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwarf something is to make it look tiny beside something bigger.

clue.text: Challenged father about being put inside

indicators.note: being put inside says the word for about goes within the word for father

parts.note: dad is father
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Dad was challenged about being sent to prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being put inside' sounds like going to jail, but it is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To dare someone is to challenge them to do something bold.

clue.text: An exciting episode, but wildly vaunted about

indicators.note: wildly signals the letters of vaunted are scattered into a new order

parts.note: re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Someone boasted extravagantly about a thrilling escapade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wildly' rearranges VAUNTED to ADVENTU, followed by RE.
explanation.definitionFit: A daring, thrilling experience or undertaking is an escapade.

clue.text: A fluorescent beetle the police would like to catch

definitions.text: the police would like to catch

explanation.surface: A glowing insect is wanted by the police.
explanation.definitionFit: Insects that glow, such as fireflies, are nicknamed this; it is also slang for an arsonist sought by detectives.

clue.text: Fought one as a matter of honour?

definitions.text: Fought one as a matter of honour?

parts.words: Fought one as a matter of honour?
parts.note: suggests a single fight for principle, but describes the formal pistol or sword contest gentlemen staged to settle insults

explanation.surface: Someone fought a single bout to defend his good name.
explanation.definitionFit: Two gentlemen settling a slight met in formal combat with pistols or swords.

clue.text: Fliers' home atmosphere gets deplorable

parts.note: the atmosphere is the air around us
base means low and contemptible, i.e. deplorable

explanation.surface: The mood at an aviators' station has turned grim.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilots and their aircraft are housed at a military station for flying.

clue.text: Defeat the other side

explanation.surface: A loss suffered by the opposing team.
explanation.definitionFit: A reverse is a setback or defeat; the reverse of a coin or page is its back or opposite face.

clue.text: Impecunious worker employed to make notes fast

parts.note: someone impecunious is short of money
a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand

explanation.surface: A poorly paid labourer is taken on as a note-taker.
explanation.definitionFit: Shorthand is a system of abbreviated symbols that lets a stenographer take dictation quickly.

clue.text: Prize man

explanation.surface: A man who has won an award.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nobel is a famous international award; Alfred Nobel was the Swedish chemist who endowed it.

clue.text: Celebrated without Heath?

parts.note: no means having none of, i.e. without
Edward Heath, UK prime minister 1970-74, was widely known as Ted

explanation.surface: A party held with the former prime minister absent.
explanation.walkthrough: Ted Heath was a British Conservative prime minister of the 1970s; 'without Ted' gives NO TED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone famous is well known and renowned.

clue.text: A deviation so Royal Artillery erupted wildly

indicators.note: wildly says the gathered letters are thrown into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: The Royal Artillery's guns erupted wildly, which was unusual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so' is a link. 'wildly' rearranges RA and ERUPTED together.
explanation.definitionFit: Straying from the usual course or plan is a departure from it.

clue.text: Diagnosed sick, but not very wisely

definitions.note: an adverbial phrase defining a hyphenated adjective, as in a decision made unwisely

parts.note: ill means sick
a doctor diagnosing a patient has judged their condition

explanation.surface: A patient was declared sick, but the call was a poor one.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads 'judged ill'; the answer puts the two pieces the other way round.
explanation.definitionFit: A poorly considered act is one taken without good judgement or thought.

clue.text: Hens usually like greenfly

explanation.surface: Hens are usually fond of greenfly.
explanation.definitionFit: Female birds are hens; the spotted beetles generally enjoy eating aphids such as greenfly.

clue.text: Plotted against getting prised apart

parts.note: con is the case against, as in pros and cons

indicators.note: prised apart means the letters of prised are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Something was schemed against, then forced open with a crowbar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apart' is the anagram signal, and 'getting' only joins the pieces; 'Plotted against' looks like one phrase but splits after the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Conspirators secretly scheme together to bring about an unlawful act.

clue.text: West Indian sort of lays cop out

indicators.note: out signals the letters of lays cop are put out of their order

explanation.surface: A Caribbean type knocks out a policeman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges LAYS COP.
explanation.definitionFit: Calypso is a style of Caribbean song from Trinidad.

clue.text: Fresh entrance to the old prison

parts.note: new means fresh
a gate is an entrance

explanation.surface: A new doorway is fitted at the former jail.
explanation.walkthrough: Newgate was a notorious London prison, demolished in 1904.
explanation.definitionFit: Newgate was a historic London jail, closed and demolished long ago.

clue.text: Plant deep in problem Bedfordshire

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words problem Bedfordshire

explanation.surface: A gardener describes setting something deep in a troublesome patch of Bedfordshire soil.
explanation.walkthrough: Bedfordshire is an English county north of London.
explanation.definitionFit: To set something firmly into a surrounding mass is to fix it deep within it.

clue.text: It gives its name to channel port

definitions.text: It gives its name to channel port

parts.words: It gives its name to channel port
parts.note: describes a western English port city that shares its name with the sea inlet beside it

explanation.surface: A harbour town lends its name to a stretch of sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bristol Channel is the inlet between south Wales and south-west England; 'channel' is not the English Channel.
explanation.definitionFit: The city on the Avon names the inlet of the Severn estuary beside it.

clue.text: Stubborn conservative did hear in his own way

indicators.note: in his own way means the letters of did hear are arranged after his own fashion

explanation.surface: A stubborn traditionalist heard things only as he chose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in his own way' rearranges DID HEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who resists change to the end is an unyielding traditionalist.

clue.text: In new role women let down

indicators.note: In places the women abbreviation inside the rearranged letters
new tells us the word role takes a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Women given a fresh part are disappointed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns ROLE into LOER and 'In' puts W inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To let something down is to bring it down from a higher position.

clue.text: Blame apportioned to, team here

indicators.note: apportioned means shared out, so the letters of blame are dealt into a new order

parts.note: a side is a sports team

explanation.surface: Fault is divided among the players, here.
explanation.walkthrough: AMBLESIDE is a small town in the English Lake District; 'here' points at the whole answer as a place. 'apportioned' rearranges BLAME to AMBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is a place name, so the bare pointer word stands for the town itself.

clue.text: Check the accuracy of someone else's account

definitions.text: Check the accuracy of someone else's account

parts.words: Check the accuracy of someone else's account
parts.note: reads like testing a person's story, but describes an accountant's formal inspection of financial books

explanation.surface: Verify whether another person's story is true.
explanation.definitionFit: An inspector formally examines a firm's financial records for errors.

clue.text: Nigel running riot in Scotland.

indicators.note: running riot means behaving wildly, so the letters of Nigel are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Nigel ran wild in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: Elgin is a town in Moray, north-east Scotland. 'running riot' rearranges NIGEL.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is a Scottish town, so the place pointer stands for it.

clue.text: Terribly bothered by how old Egyptians suffered

explanation.surface: Ancient Egyptians were sorely troubled.
explanation.definitionFit: Plagued means harassed or tormented; in Exodus Egypt was struck by ten plagues.

clue.text: Great at organised water sports

indicators.note: organised means arranged in order, so the letters of great at are set out afresh

explanation.surface: Aquatic athletes are good at being organised.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowing or sailing meeting is a programme of boat races on water.

clue.text: In public early starters tuck in too much

indicators.note: In tells us the early starters go inside the word for public

parts.note: something overt is done in public, openly
the first two letters of the word early are E and A

explanation.surface: Diners who come early to a public meal stuff themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'early starters' takes the opening letters of 'early', EA, which go into OVERT.
explanation.definitionFit: To gorge is to eat beyond what is needed.

clue.text: One picked out

parts.note: reads as a person chosen, but describes someone chosen alone

explanation.surface: A single person chosen from a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: To be chosen individually from a group is to be selected for special attention.
